page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d2s.5xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 10 physical Intel Xeon 8163 processor cores running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 88.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.4 GB per core, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. A key hardware characteristic is its massive bundled local storage capacity of 62,706 GB delivered via HDD.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 ranking in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core scaling is average, as demonstrated by middle-tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is average for both small and large block reads and writes, though the Passmark memory score itself is weak.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.d2s.5xlarge is its reliance on high-capacity HDD local storage coupled with modest single-core compute capabilities. This makes it highly cost-efficient for storage-dense workloads that require massive capacity rather than high-speed IOPS or extreme CPU performance. It is well-suited for large-scale data warehousing, log processing, distributed file systems, and database operations that can leverage multi-threaded processing and require substantial local storage volume.
